headline: Claude Code automatically creates narrated product demos, syncing audio to video without manual editing
summary: An AI agent leverages Playwright and ElevenLabs to record web apps, write narration, and perfectly align voiceovers with on-screen actions, eliminating manual video production.
details: Claude Code, an AI agent, can automatically generate narrated product demo videos, as demonstrated by a solo builder for their ClinTrialFinder web app. This process eliminates manual screen recording, voiceover, and video editing.

The agent uses a Playwright script to drive the live web app headless, recording the entire interaction directly to video. This code-driven approach ensures deterministic and repeatable recordings, even injecting a fake cursor for clarity.

For narration, the agent writes the script and then synthesizes the voiceover using the ElevenLabs text-to-speech API. This allows for instant changes and regeneration of audio clips without re-recording.

The truly innovative part is the automatic audio-video synchronization. While recording, the agent logs timestamps of key on-screen events, then cuts the narration into phrases and places them precisely at the corresponding timestamps using `ffmpeg`.
This transforms video production from a four-step manual process (screen-record, script, voiceover, sync) into a single conversation with an AI agent. The entire pipeline is automated and code-based.
The agent also handles complex technical issues, such as adapting to sites that don't render headless or managing audio mixing, without requiring human intervention or debugging.

This approach is not specific to the ClinTrialFinder project; any web application can benefit from an AI agent generating a narrated, synced demo video without the need for manual recording or editing tools.

headline_marked: [[Firefox is now the last major browser that still supports uBlock Origin]]
headline: Firefox is now the last major browser that still supports uBlock Origin
summary: Microsoft Edge is set to block uBlock Origin with its Manifest V3 migration, following Google's lead for Chromium-based browsers. This leaves Firefox as the sole major browser maintaining full support.
details: Firefox recently confirmed its continued support for uBlock Origin, stating via Bluesky that its "support for uBlock Origin isn’t going anywhere." This announcement comes as other major browsers are moving away from the extension.

Microsoft Edge is preparing to block uBlock Origin and similar ad-blocking extensions that rely on the Manifest V2 architecture. Once Edge transitions to Manifest V3, these extensions will lose the necessary functions to effectively identify and block ads.

This shift by Microsoft Edge aligns with Google's initiative. Edge is built on Chromium, the open-source browser engine that powers most modern web browsers, and Google began the Manifest V2 to V3 migration in Chrome/Chromium.

Firefox stands out as one of the few web browsers not based on Chromium. It is now the only major browser that still offers full support for uBlock Origin, distinguishing it from Safari and DuckDuckGo, which also do not support the extension.

For users prioritizing uBlock Origin, Firefox now presents itself as the only major browser without compromises. Other browsers will either require settling for a less-featured uBlock Origin Lite or relying on their built-in ad-blocking capabilities.
